Mike Corder reported from The Hague, Netherlands, and Jill Lawless from London. Justin Spike contributed to this report from Budapest, Hungary.

Support trusted journalism and civil dialogue.

By Daniel Niemann, Jill Lawless, Mike Corder, Associated Press [...] STOCKHOLM (AP) — Hungarian writer László Krasznahorkai, whose philosophical, bleakly funny novels often unfold in single sentences, won the Nobel Prize in literature Thursday for his "compelling and visionary oeuvre that, in the midst of apocalyptic terror, reaffirms the power of art."

Watch the announcement in our video player above.

Several works including his debut, "Satantango" and "The Melancholy of Resistance," were turned into films by Hungarian director Béla Tarr.
